blocks.x: Applied AI & GenAI applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Agriculture & Food Systems, applied ai & generative ai at dataq soft covers the full lifecycle of enterprise intelligence: strategy and value mapping, platform build-out, model adaptation, retrieval architectures, multimodal systems, and the governance fabric that keeps every model auditable. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: enterprise ai strategy & roadmapping, generative ai platform engineering, llm fine-tuning & model operations — delivered on Dataq Compass and Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Harvest forecasting is regional guesswork; quality attributes (protein, moisture, defects) are discovered at intake, not predicted.
Agronomic decisions run on tradition because soil, weather and crop telemetry are patchy; input spend is uniform where it should be variable.
Origin, organic and deforestation-free claims face EUDR-grade scrutiny; evidence is paper and trust.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 7 services from the Applied AI & Generative AI tower — Enterprise AI Strategy & Roadmapping, Generative AI Platform Engineering, LLM Fine-Tuning & Model Operations, RAG & Enterprise Knowledge Systems as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: GDPR obligations shape the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Align AI to P&L lines and risk mandates — a sequenced portfolio, not a pile of pilots.
One governed platform, many GenAI products: retrieval, guardrails and cost control as shared services.
Own your models: tune, distill and operate LLMs with measurable quality, controlled cost and enforceable policy.
Answers with citations, not vibes: permission-aware retrieval over your regulated document estate.
Satellite+sensor+agronomy models per field with uncertainty bands (harvest and trading decisions informed early)
Field-grounded recommendations with treatment citations for advisors (advisory coverage extended per agronomist)

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: GDPR and EUDR. Deforestation-free due diligence with geolocation evidence for in-scope commodities. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
